note: Typed routes. One row per way Forge can reach a tool, whatever kind of thing it is. Kind 'mcp' names a SERVER the host connects to; kind 'process' names a COMMAND the host runs. Rows are host-neutral by construction and never carry a host's spelling of a tool namespace, so adding a host never edits this file and adding a route never edits host code.
rules: Every id must match a dependency id in catalog.json. One dependency truth, not two.
A row declares kind. 'mcp' requires server; 'process' requires command. Nothing else varies by kind, so a route of either kind is probed, scored, leased and reported the same way.
A row grants tools only to an agent that declares the matching capability, and only on a host that provides every entry in requires_host_provides.
A row without a resolvable probe is not routable. Detection is never assumed from installation.
fallbacks must name the same route catalog.json declares for the dependency, so a missing route degrades instead of blocking.
Lane ids carry a lane. prefix. Capability ids never do, so a lane and a capability cannot collide in the same namespace.

Routes whose lanes share an exclusive group in .forge/state/leases.json can never hold their lanes at once. The live editor and the closed editor are the same project, so running one blocks the other by construction rather than by convention.

A row that contends for a shared resource names the lease it takes. The lease must appear in an exclusive group in .forge/state/leases.json, so the route registry and the ledger that enforces exclusion use one vocabulary instead of two that happen to agree.

probe_kinds.mcp-server-declared: The server id appears in an MCP client configuration the host declares in hosts/registry.json mcp.config_paths. Read-only: it inspects configuration and never starts, installs, or contacts a server.
probe_kinds.mcp-http-handshake: The server answers an MCP initialize request at its declared http endpoint. Contacts a server already running on this machine; never starts, installs, or writes anything. A pass is evidence the route is live, so it earns AVAILABLE_VERIFIED where a declaration alone earns only AVAILABLE_UNVERIFIED.
probe_kinds.ue-commandlet-ready: The engine's editor-closed command is resolvable AND the live editor is not holding the project. Readiness is the inverse of mcp-http-handshake: this route requires the editor's MCP endpoint to be silent, because a commandlet must not run against a project the live editor has open. Resolving the command is not a round trip, so a clear lane earns AVAILABLE_UNVERIFIED and only an acceptance suite earns more.

lanes.lane.ue-editor: Live Unreal editor session. Exclusive: native typed calls, live scripting and human editor work all contend for it.
lanes.lane.ue-editor-closed: Editor-closed Unreal API: UnrealEditor-Cmd, Python commandlets and batch operations against a project no live editor holds. Mutually exclusive with every live-editor lane through the project super-lock, and the first choice for batch import, retargeting, large asset audits, LOD generation, null-RHI-safe work and anything unsafe inside the live editor tick.
lanes.lane.dcc-authoring: External DCC authoring session. Runs concurrently with ue.editor because it writes intermediate assets, not the project.

providers.implementation: Unreal Engine's first-party Unreal MCP plugin (ModelContextProtocol), Experimental since 5.8. The editor hosts the server; Forge never starts it.

requires_engine.note: ModelContextProtocol serves the endpoint; without AllToolsets it advertises no tools. The editor must be open for the route to answer.

providers.tool_surface: Discovery mode by default: list_toolsets, describe_toolset and call_tool stand in for the full tool set, so the schema stays small. Treat named tools as discovered at runtime, never as a fixed contract.

providers.implementation: Optional live-Python accelerator inside the open editor: arbitrary unreal.*, VibeUE skills and service wrappers, GeometryScript, materials and properties the first-party typed toolsets do not expose. Not a prerequisite; it earns its place when its probe shows live Python closing a real route gap.

requires_engine.note: Runs inside the open editor's Python, so it needs the editor up and PythonScriptPlugin enabled.

providers.tool_surface: Arbitrary unreal.* execution. Never used for known re-entrant or heavy operations: those belong on lane.ue-editor-closed, where a commandlet cannot corrupt a live editor tick.

providers.implementation: Unreal's editor-closed Python and commandlet surface, driven through UnrealEditor-Cmd. A primary production surface, not a degraded one: it reaches the batch and bulk operations the live typed route does not expose and must not attempt inside the editor tick.

requires_engine.note: PythonScriptPlugin serves the unreal.* API; EditorScriptingUtilities serves the editor operations most batch work calls. Neither requires the editor to be open.

providers.tool_surface: A script plus a result file. The result file is the authority on what happened; an exit code alone is not, because a commandlet can exit zero having failed the work.
